Bill.BriefDescription: Preserving rail facilities and railroads by retaining and reusing rail and crossing material.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to rail preservation; reenacting and amending RCW43.79A.040; adding new sections to chapter 47.01 RCW; creating a newsection; and providing an expiration date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that there areinsufficient resources for public or privately owned rail systems toadequately address rail infrastructure needs. Rail material that canbe used for priority rail projects either sits idle, is sold for scrap,or is shipped out of state. The legislature also finds that where railrelated operations orfacilities benefit or have benefited from public investment throughgrants, loans, tax relief, or partnerships with local, state, orfederal governments or port districts, there is a public interest inensuring that available rail and crossing materials be retained andreused to modify or improve existing rail facilities. It is the intent of the legislature to retain and reuse railmaterial that becomes available within the state to restore, preserve,and enhance rail facilities in order to preserve the use of railroadsfor freight, passengers, and economic development.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 47.01 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The rail preservation pilot project is established within thedepartment of transportation to make rail and crossing materialsavailable to instate rail operators or owners of public or privatelyowned short line or mainline rail facilities. (2) The department of transportation shall establish eligibilitycriteria to award instate rail operators or owners of public orprivately owned short line or mainline rail facilities rail andcrossing materials. The criteria must include, but is not limited to: (a) Receipt of competitive state or federal grants or loans; (b) Approval by credible expert analysis; (c) Impending new opportunities for rail use and expansion; (d) Receipt of prior public investment; (e) Safety record; and (f) Inkind or cash investments or local matching funds. (3) The department shall consider the instate value of rail andcrossing material available when investing in rail improvement projectsand seek methods to make reusable rail and crossing material availableto preserve and improve instate rail facilities. (4) Where public funds are used to improve, replace, or enhance arail facility, the department must offer any rail and crossing materialremoved from the facility to other rail improvement projects withinWashington state before the sale or removal of the rail materialoutside of the state.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 47.01 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The department shall establish the rail material reuse grantprogram. Through this program the department shall provide grants andtechnical assistance to instate rail operators or owners of public orprivately owned rail facilities. The grants are to be used for theacquisition, removal, and transport of reusable and salvageable railand crossing material by the instate rail operators or owners. Thetechnical assistance is to help the instate rail operators or ownersapply for grants and carry out the program. To be eligible for grantsunder this program, the recipient instate rail operator or owner must HB 1815 p. 2 be involved in a rail improvement project listed and evaluated by thepublic transportation and rail division of the department. (2) The recipient instate rail operator or owner must place thegrants and matching funds in a revolving loan fund and deposit them ina bank or savings institution in an account that is separate from allother funds of the recipient. The funds and interest earned on thesefunds must be utilized only to acquire, remove, and transport reusableand salvageable rail and crossing material.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 47.01 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The rail preservation fund is created in the custody of the statetreasurer. All receipts from federal or state grants and loansreceived by the department of transportation for rail improvementproject purposes must be deposited into the fund. Expenditures fromthe fund may be used only to supply instate rail operators or ownersof public and privately owned short line and mainline rail facilitieswith rail and crossing materials. Only the secretary of transportationor the secretary's designee may authorize expenditures from the fund.The fund is subject to allotment procedures under chapter 43.88 RCW,but an appropriation is not required for expenditures.

(2) All income received from investment of the treasurer's trustfund shall be set aside in an account in the treasury trust fund to beknown as the investment income account. (3) The investment income account may be utilized for the paymentof purchased banking services on behalf of treasurer's trust fundsincluding, but not limited to, depository, safekeeping, anddisbursement functions for the state treasurer or affected stateagencies.
